sections.title: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.blurb: 22 questions, 40 minutes. Arithmetic alone is roughly a third of the paper, so the path starts there and builds up through numbers, algebra, geometry and modern math.

topics.title: Arithmetic
topics.blurb: The highest-weightage area in CAT (typically 7–9 of 22 questions). Everything here is built on one skill: translating a word problem into a ratio.

concepts.title: Percentages
concepts.blurb: Percent as a fraction, successive changes, the multiplying-factor method, percentage points vs percent.

concepts.title: Ratio & Proportion
concepts.blurb: Scaling ratios, combining ratios, variation (direct, inverse, joint) and partnership problems.

concepts.title: Averages
concepts.blurb: Average as a balance point, the deviation method, weighted averages, and what happens when items join or leave a group.

concepts.title: Alligation & Mixtures
concepts.blurb: The weighted-average rule turned into a one-line tool; replacement problems and mixing two mixtures.

concepts.title: Profit, Loss & Discount
concepts.blurb: Cost, mark-up, discount and profit as a chain of multiplying factors; faulty weights and successive discounts.

concepts.title: Simple & Compound Interest
concepts.blurb: SI as linear growth, CI as repeated percentage growth, the SI–CI difference shortcut, and instalments.

concepts.title: Time, Speed & Distance
concepts.blurb: Proportionality is the whole chapter: relative speed, trains, boats and streams, circular tracks and races.

concepts.title: Time & Work
concepts.blurb: Work as units via LCM, efficiency, pipes and cisterns, and people leaving or joining mid-way.

topics.title: Number Systems
topics.blurb: Two or three questions a year, but the ideas (divisibility, remainders, factor counting) quietly power many algebra and counting questions.

concepts.title: Divisibility & Remainders
concepts.blurb: Divisibility rules, remainder arithmetic, negative remainders, and cyclicity of remainders.

concepts.title: Factors, HCF & LCM
concepts.blurb: Prime factorisation as the master key: counting factors, sum of factors, HCF/LCM and their relation.

concepts.title: Last Digits & Cyclicity
concepts.blurb: Units digit of powers, last two digits, and the pattern-spotting mindset behind them.

concepts.title: Factorials & Trailing Zeros
concepts.blurb: Highest power of a prime in n!, trailing zeros, and factorial-based digit questions.

concepts.title: Integer Solutions of Equations
concepts.blurb: Counting integer solutions of linear equations with bounds; a favourite CAT TITA format.

topics.title: Algebra
topics.blurb: Five to seven questions a year. CAT algebra is not about long manipulation but about spotting the structure (symmetry, substitution, bounds).

concepts.title: Linear Equations & Inequalities
concepts.blurb: Setting up and solving systems, inequality rules, and integer constraints that turn inequalities into counting.

concepts.title: Quadratic Equations
concepts.blurb: Roots, discriminant, sum and product of roots, forming equations from roots, and nature of roots.

concepts.title: Algebraic Identities & Substitution
concepts.blurb: The identities CAT actually uses, symmetric expressions, and the 'let t = …' substitution reflex.

concepts.title: Modulus, Functions & Graphs
concepts.blurb: Absolute value as distance, piecewise reasoning, function composition, and reading graphs.

concepts.title: Logarithms
concepts.blurb: The three log rules, change of base, and log equations that are really exponent equations.

concepts.title: Progressions (AP, GP, HP)
concepts.blurb: nth term and sum formulas, the middle-term trick, and infinite GP.

concepts.title: Maxima & Minima (AM–GM and friends)
concepts.blurb: AM ≥ GM, completing the square, and bounding expressions without calculus.

topics.title: Geometry & Mensuration
topics.blurb: Four to six questions a year. Triangles and circles carry most of the weight; mensuration is formula recall plus ratio sense.

concepts.title: Lines, Angles & Triangle Basics
concepts.blurb: Angle facts, triangle inequality, special triangles (30-60-90, 45-45-90), and area formulas.

concepts.title: Similar Triangles
concepts.blurb: Similarity criteria, ratio of areas, basic proportionality theorem, and the right-triangle altitude relations.

concepts.title: Circles
concepts.blurb: Chords, tangents, inscribed angles, cyclic quadrilaterals, and the chord–tangent power of a point.

concepts.title: Quadrilaterals & Polygons
concepts.blurb: Parallelograms, trapezia, regular polygons, interior angles and area relations.

concepts.title: Coordinate Geometry
concepts.blurb: Distance, section formula, lines (slope, intercepts), area of triangle, and circles in the plane.

concepts.title: Mensuration (2D & 3D)
concepts.blurb: Areas and volumes of standard solids, cones and frustums, and ratio shortcuts for scaled shapes.

topics.title: Modern Math
topics.blurb: Two to four questions a year, usually of medium difficulty: counting, probability and Venn diagrams.

concepts.title: Permutations & Combinations
concepts.blurb: Counting principle, arrangements vs selections, grouping with constraints, and distribution (stars and bars).

concepts.title: Probability
concepts.blurb: Probability as favourable/total, complementary counting, and independent vs dependent events.

concepts.title: Set Theory & Venn Diagrams
concepts.blurb: Two- and three-set formulas, max/min of overlaps, and the 'at least / exactly' bookkeeping.

sections.title: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension
sections.blurb: 24 questions, 40 minutes. Four RC passages (16 questions) plus 8 verbal ability questions. Accuracy, not speed, separates 95 from 99 percentile here.

topics.title: Reading Comprehension
topics.blurb: Two-thirds of the section. Learn to read for structure first, then attack each question type with a specific method.

concepts.title: Reading a CAT Passage
concepts.blurb: How to read for structure: paragraph roles, author's position, and building a 30-second mental map.

concepts.title: Main Idea & Primary Purpose
concepts.blurb: Distinguishing the central claim from supporting detail; scope traps (too broad, too narrow).

concepts.title: Inference Questions
concepts.blurb: What the passage must imply vs what merely sounds plausible; the 'one step only' rule.

concepts.title: Tone, Attitude & Author's Stance
concepts.blurb: Reading tone from word choice, hedging language, and the difference between describing and endorsing.

concepts.title: Specific Detail & Vocabulary in Context
concepts.blurb: Locating and paraphrasing; word-meaning questions where the dictionary meaning is the trap.

concepts.title: Application, Strengthen & Weaken
concepts.blurb: Extending the author's logic to new situations; which option would the author agree with.

concepts.title: Elimination & Option Analysis
concepts.blurb: The four ways a wrong option is wrong: extreme, out of scope, distortion, opposite.

topics.title: Verbal Ability
topics.blurb: Eight questions, mostly TITA (no negative marking) — para-jumbles, odd sentence out, and the MCQ para-summary.

concepts.title: Para-jumbles
concepts.blurb: Finding the opening sentence, mandatory pairs via pronouns/connectors, and chronology.

concepts.title: Odd Sentence Out
concepts.blurb: Spotting the sentence that breaks the paragraph's thread; theme vs detail mismatch.

concepts.title: Para-summary
concepts.blurb: Compressing a paragraph to its claim; rejecting summaries that add, drop or distort.

concepts.title: Para-completion
concepts.blurb: Choosing the sentence that fits a gap by logic, tone and reference.

sections.title: Data Interpretation & Logical Reasoning
sections.blurb: 20 questions in 4 sets, 40 minutes. The section that decides calls: pick 2–3 doable sets, nail them fully, and leave the rest.

topics.title: Foundations & Set Selection
topics.blurb: Before any set type: how to scan all four sets in 5 minutes, choose, and manage time.

concepts.title: Set Selection & Time Strategy
concepts.blurb: Judging a set by its data density and question types; the 'attempt 2 fully' plan.

concepts.title: Speed Calculation for DI
concepts.blurb: Approximation, percentage change by eye, ratio comparison, and when exactness matters.

topics.title: Data Interpretation
topics.blurb: Tables, charts and reasoning-heavy DI. Modern CAT DI is less about calculation and more about deducing missing data.

concepts.title: Tables, Bar & Line Charts
concepts.blurb: Reading data fast, computing growth and share, and spotting what the question really asks.

concepts.title: Reasoning-based DI (Missing Data)
concepts.blurb: Using totals, ranks and constraints to fill a partially given table.

concepts.title: Venn Diagram based DI
concepts.blurb: Three-set Venns with max/min, and set data presented as tables.

concepts.title: Games & Tournaments
concepts.blurb: Round-robin and knockout structures, points tables, and deducing results from standings.

topics.title: Logical Reasoning
topics.blurb: Arrangements, distributions and puzzles. The skill is representing constraints visually and reasoning from the most restrictive one first.

concepts.title: Linear & Circular Arrangements
concepts.blurb: Seating and ordering with constraints; using the most restrictive clue first.

concepts.title: Grouping & Distribution
concepts.blurb: Assigning people to teams, items to boxes, with counts and exclusions.

concepts.title: Scheduling & Sequencing
concepts.blurb: Timetables, days-and-slots grids, and ordering events with before/after clues.

concepts.title: Selection with Constraints
concepts.blurb: Choosing a subset under if-then rules; case trees and contradiction.

concepts.title: Routes & Networks
concepts.blurb: Paths, flows and shortest routes in a diagram; counting paths with restrictions.

concepts.title: Quant-based Puzzles
concepts.blurb: LR sets where the constraints are numerical: sums, ranks, averages in a grid.
